To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a complex intervention for supporting carers of patients receiving chemotherapy, co-designed by staff, patients, and carers, was acceptable, feasible, and showed promise in improving knowledge and coping.

a complex intervention co-produced by carers and HCs to support carers of patients undergoing chemotherapy is acceptable to carers, HCPs and patients, feasible to deliver in the chemotherapy outpatient environment and shows promising effects in improving carers’ knowledge of chemotherapy and side effects and meeting their information needs.

the ‘Take Care’, a novel intervention designed by staff and carer co-designers, is feasible and acceptable for carers of patients undergoing chemotherapy and has the potential to increase carers’ knowledge, confidence and satisfaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the experiences of carers of patients receiving chemotherapy.
improving the quality of care provided by NHS hospitals to carers.
the development and evaluation of a new intervention for carers of people with cancer who are undergoing chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intervention was feasible and acceptable and demonstrated some promise of effectiveness.
the ‘Take Care intervention’ is feasible and acceptable and has the potential to improve the care of carers of people with cancer.
the ‘Take Care intervention’ is a feasible complex intervention which is acceptable to carers, and that the study design and processes were acceptable to participants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intervention is acceptable, feasible and has potential for effectiveness.
the intervention is a complex one that has been co-designed with carers.
the study was a success and the intervention was acceptable and useful.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carers and HCFs were willing to participate and found the intervention acceptable.
it is possible to design an intervention with carers that is acceptable to them and HCPs.
carers need to be supported in a holistic way and that a one-size-fits-all approach is unlikely to be effective.
